liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Dark Star** (3 reviews): Reviewer also praises the Dark Star into El Paso into jam sequence; Reviewer likes the first-set Dark Star into El Paso back into Dark Star, calling it a cool little sequence [8][10][16]
- **Not Fade Away** (2 reviews): Reviewer calls the Not Fade Away jam mindblowing, with crisp, exact playing from Jerry and a band fully engaged; Around 3:59 of the jam, Bobby plays the classic China Cat riff in his higher-register rhythm work [8][19]
- **Playin' In The Band** (1 review): Playin' has intense jamming, starting to stretch out toward its 1972-74 heyday [15]
- **Jack Straw** (1 review): Reviewer singles out Jack Straw and Loser as incredible versions [13]
- **Cumberland Blues** (1 review): Reviewer describes Cumberland as blazing, and Brokedown Palace as a great version [12]

## Setlist highlights

- **Looney Tunes**: mythic rare: 2 archived performances [20]

## The recordings

- **gd1971-11-15.sbd.unknown.31607.flac16** (recommended): soundboard; 25 songs; 148 min; rated 4.42/5 by 12 [1]
- **gd71-11-15.sbd.cotsman.12438.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 26 songs; 149 min; rated 4.37/5 by 19 [2]. Said about its sound: Sound isn't crystal clear but is warm, smooth and ragged, like a favorite woolen carpet; Mostly great sound apart from a few short bits from another source; Garcia's guitar resembles the Skull and Roses recording; Mix is clear: every Bobby note audible, Phil thundering, Keith sparkling with honkytonk feel; Billy could be somewhat higher [13][14]
- **gd1971-11-15.163803.fm.zavislak.miller.clugston.flac16**: FM broadcast; 25 songs; 150 min [3]
- **gd1971-11-15.sbd.set2.jupille.7735.shnf**: soundboard; 8 songs; 56 min; rated 3.9/5 by 10 [7]

## Around the show

- Pigpen was being treated for liver problems and absent from the fall 1971 tour, returning Dec. 1 after leaving following Aug. 26 [9]
- Band played as a five-piece (Phil, Billy, Jerry, Bobby, Keith) without Pigpen, adding newer songs like Jack Straw and Ramble On Rose [12]
- Reviewer finds this Not Fade Away's free jam worthy of the best '72 Dark Stars [11]
- Dark Stars in 1971 were shorter and less exploratory than earlier or later years; only eight were played that year [12]
- Reviewer says this Dark Star has almost a 1972 sound, without Donna [16]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1971-11-15.sbd.unknown.31607.flac16**: source: MSR>C>DAT2x>Delta Dio 2496>Soundforge>WAV>FLAC [1]
- **gd71-11-15.sbd.cotsman.12438.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [2]. Also: Soundboard patched with slightly degraded soundboard; lineage includes one cassette generation, then CD and EAC to SHN [2]
- **gd1971-11-15.163803.fm.zavislak.miller.clugston.flac16**: taped by Matthew Zavislak; transferred by Scott Clugston, Charlie Miller; source: FM Broadcast > Unknown gear > ?? > DAT (16/44.1) [3]
- **gd1971-11-15.sbd.set2.jupille.7735.shnf**: transferred by David Gans and Joe Jupille; source: SBD:MR > Cassette > Sonic Solutions > CDR > EAC > SHN [7]. Also: Set two soundboard CD mastered by David Gans, then extracted with EAC and encoded to shn [7]

## Art and photos

- Fan art by Music on TIDAL: [Grateful Dead - Road Trips Vol. 3 No. 2: Municipal Auditorium, Austin, TX 11/15/71 (Live)](https://tidal.com/album/24733046) [27]
